links.outcome: Staff trust and distrust in ML-based clinical decision support after receiving basic information versus controls
links.effect: Versus active control: trust +5% (95% CI 2%; 9%), p<0.001; distrust -4% (-7%; -1%), p=0.042. Versus blank control: trust +5% (2%; 11%), p=0.003; distrust -3% (-6%; -1%), p=0.021.
links.quote: Providing information on ML-based clinical decision support systems in hospital psychiatry may increase healthcare staff trust in such systems.

links.effect: Trust +5%, p<0.001 vs active control and +5%, p=0.003 vs blank; distrust -4%, p=0.042 and -3%, p=0.021.
links.quote: The intervention enhanced trust and diminished distrust in ML-based clinical decision support systems compared with the active control arm (Trust: mean difference= 5% [95% confidence interval (CI): 2%; 9%], p-value < 0.001; Distrust: mean difference=-4% [-7%; -1%], p-value = 0.042)) and the blank control arm (Trust: mean difference= 5% [2%; 11%], p-value = 0.003; Distrust: mean difference= -3% [-6%; - 1%], p-value = 0.021).

links.outcome: Healthcare staff trust and distrust in ML-based clinical decision support systems
links.effect: Trust increased 5% vs active control (p < 0.001) and 5% vs blank control (p = 0.003); distrust decreased 4% vs active control (p = 0.042) and 3% vs blank control (p = 0.021).
